summary: base_parts_ai self-updates by fetching and globally installing an unverified tarball from an author-controlled Aliyun OSS bucket on every CLI run
details: On every invocation of the package's CLIs (jcc/jcx/ucx/jgrok and related entry points), lib/ai_utils.js fetches a JSON config from https://jai.jaskle.cn/hm/hm_pub/ai_cc_cfg and reads a server-supplied newVer field. When newVer is greater than the installed version, the code builds a tarball URL of the form https://jdwfiles.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/npm_pkg/base_parts_ai-<newVer>.tgz and passes it to pkgCmd.execGlobalCmd, which runs `npm install -g <tgz-url> --registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com --force`. The user confirmation prompt is commented out and the confirmed flag is hardcoded to "yes", so the global install proceeds without interaction. The update source is not the npm registry — it is a mutable author-controlled Aliyun OSS object whose contents can be changed server-side at any time with no registry review, no version pinning, and no hash or signature check. lib/pkg_cmd.js additionally constructs the strings 'npm install', '--registry=', and '--force' at runtime by XOR-decoding (String.fromCharCode(b ^ 0x5A)) hardcoded byte arrays rather than storing the commands as plain literals, concealing the install mechanism from static scanners. Running any CLI from this package therefore causes global installation of whatever bytes the author (or anyone who compromises jai.jaskle.cn or the jdwfiles Aliyun OSS bucket) serves at that URL at that moment, yielding arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
